calls.reason: Inner Monologue shows feedback improves LLM robot planning and HoloMind shows progress with many failures, but nothing isolates world comprehension as the cause, and success has no defined threshold.
WIRED reports Everyday Robots shut down in Feb 2023. Four years later the packet shows only research such as Gemini Robotics, and no PaLM-SayCan product or direct derivative.
The forecast is hedged ('don't hold our breath') and the interpreted 2027 deadline hasn't passed. Figure's 56% success rate and NEO's undelivered status lean his way but don't decide it.

The SayCan paper admits a negation failure inherited from its language model, and a 2022 robotics paper treats catastrophic forgetting as a live problem. Both support the modest claim of no exemption.
The claim has no deadline. Data-scaling studies and π0.7 show gains without isolating data as sufficient or ruling it out, so the outcome is still open.
SayCan's Appendix E.3 Table 8 reports a drawer restocking task with 1.0 planning and 0.0 execution, which fits the 33% overall execution rate. So at least one PaLM-SayCan task scored zero.
